parts.title: Part 1 — The disease cards
parts.blurb: Every word of text the app shows on a disease card. **The two fields to check first are Prevent and Treat**: they are the only place the app comes close to saying what a person should do, they are read by children, and a wrong one is the only kind of error here that could matter outside the game.

claims.subject: Influenza
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Virus isolated 1933; the 1918 pandemic killed ~50 million.

claims.subject: Influenza
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Fever, aches, cough; can lead to pneumonia and myocarditis.

claims.subject: Influenza
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide, in yearly winter waves.

claims.subject: Influenza
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Annual flu vaccine. It changes because the virus mutates fast.

claims.subject: Influenza
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Rest, fluids; antivirals for high-risk patients.

claims.subject: Influenza
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: Flu mutates fast. Last year's antibodies may not fit.

claims.subject: Common cold
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Rhinovirus identified in the 1950s.

claims.subject: Common cold
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Runny nose, sore throat, sneezing.

claims.subject: Common cold
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Everywhere, all year.

claims.subject: Common cold
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Handwashing. No vaccine. Over 100 strains.

claims.subject: Common cold
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: No cure; it passes in about a week.

claims.subject: Common cold
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: Over 100 strains; no lasting immunity.

claims.subject: COVID-19
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: SARS-CoV-2 identified in Wuhan, China, December 2019.

claims.subject: COVID-19
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Cough, fever, loss of smell; pneumonia and myocarditis in severe cases.

claims.subject: COVID-19
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide pandemic from 2020.

claims.subject: COVID-19
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Vaccination, ventilation, masks during outbreaks.

claims.subject: COVID-19
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Supportive care; antivirals for those at risk.

claims.subject: COVID-19
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: Can inflame the heart muscle (myocarditis) as well as the lungs.

claims.subject: RSV
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Respiratory syncytial virus, discovered 1956.

claims.subject: RSV
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Cold-like illness; bronchiolitis and pneumonia in babies.

claims.subject: RSV
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide, seasonal.

claims.subject: RSV
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Monoclonal antibodies and a maternal vaccine for infants.

claims.subject: RSV
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Supportive care; oxygen if severe.

claims.subject: RSV
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: Mild in adults, dangerous for babies.

claims.subject: Measles
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Vaccine by John Enders, 1963. One of the most contagious viruses known.

claims.subject: Measles
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Rash and fever. And IMMUNE AMNESIA: it wipes out your existing immune memory, leaving you open to diseases you had already beaten.

claims.subject: Measles
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide; resurges wherever vaccination drops.

claims.subject: Measles
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: MMR vaccine. Two doses.

claims.subject: Measles
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: No antiviral; vitamin A and supportive care. Prevention is everything.

claims.subject: Mumps
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Described by Hippocrates; vaccine 1967.

claims.subject: Mumps
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Swollen salivary glands; can inflame the brain and testes.

claims.subject: Mumps
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide.

claims.subject: Mumps
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: MMR vaccine.

claims.subject: Mumps
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Supportive care only.

claims.subject: Rubella
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Link to birth defects found by Norman Gregg, 1941.

claims.subject: Rubella
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Mild rash in children. But devastating to an unborn baby.

claims.subject: Rubella
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide.

claims.subject: Rubella
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: MMR vaccine, especially before pregnancy.

claims.subject: Rubella
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: No cure; prevention protects the next generation.

claims.subject: Smallpox
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Jenner's cowpox vaccine, 1796. The first vaccine ever made.

claims.subject: Smallpox
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Disfiguring pustules; killed around 30% of those infected.

claims.subject: Smallpox
claims.label: Found
claims.text: NOWHERE. Declared eradicated in 1980. The only human disease ever wiped out.

claims.subject: Smallpox
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Vaccination. The campaign that ended it.

claims.subject: Smallpox
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: None needed. This card is a trophy: proof that immunology WINS.

claims.subject: Nipah
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Identified in Malaysia 1998; outbreaks in Kerala, India (2018, 2023).

claims.subject: Nipah
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Brain inflammation; fatal in 40-75% of cases.

claims.subject: Nipah
claims.label: Found
claims.text: South and Southeast Asia; spread by fruit bats.

claims.subject: Nipah
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Avoid raw date-palm sap; isolate cases.

claims.subject: Nipah
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: No specific cure. Supportive care.

claims.subject: Hand-foot-and-mouth
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Coxsackievirus, 1950s.

claims.subject: Hand-foot-and-mouth
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Blisters on hands, feet and mouth; usually mild in children.

claims.subject: Hand-foot-and-mouth
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide; common in schools.

claims.subject: Hand-foot-and-mouth
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Handwashing.

claims.subject: Hand-foot-and-mouth
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Self-limiting.

claims.subject: Chickenpox
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Varicella-zoster; vaccine developed in the 1970s.

claims.subject: Chickenpox
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Itchy blisters. Then HIDES IN YOUR NERVES for decades and can return as shingles.

claims.subject: Chickenpox
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide.

claims.subject: Chickenpox
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Varicella vaccine.

claims.subject: Chickenpox
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antivirals if severe.

claims.subject: Chickenpox
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: Hides in nerves for decades. Returns as shingles.

claims.subject: Glandular fever
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Epstein-Barr virus, discovered 1964.

claims.subject: Glandular fever
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Fever, sore throat, extreme fatigue, swollen spleen (rupture risk).

claims.subject: Glandular fever
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide; common in teenagers.

claims.subject: Glandular fever
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: No vaccine.

claims.subject: Glandular fever
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Rest. Avoid contact sport while the spleen is swollen.

claims.subject: Glandular fever
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: Hides inside your own B-cells; risks spleen rupture.

claims.subject: Cytomegalovirus
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Isolated 1956.

claims.subject: Cytomegalovirus
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Harmless in healthy people. It just hides for life. Dangerous to babies and the immunosuppressed.

claims.subject: Cytomegalovirus
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Most adults worldwide carry it.

claims.subject: Cytomegalovirus
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Hygiene; no vaccine yet.

claims.subject: Cytomegalovirus
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antivirals only when it reactivates.

claims.subject: Tuberculosis
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Bacterium found by Robert Koch, 1882.

claims.subject: Tuberculosis
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Chronic cough, weight loss, night sweats. Can lie dormant for YEARS.

claims.subject: Tuberculosis
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide. India carries the largest burden of any country.

claims.subject: Tuberculosis
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: BCG vaccine; treating active cases; ventilation.

claims.subject: Tuberculosis
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: 6+ months of combination antibiotics. Not finishing the course breeds resistance.

claims.subject: Tuberculosis
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: Can lie dormant in the lungs for years.

claims.subject: Whooping cough
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Bordetella pertussis, identified 1906.

claims.subject: Whooping cough
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Violent coughing fits with a 'whoop'; deadly in babies.

claims.subject: Whooping cough
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide; returns where vaccination falls.

claims.subject: Whooping cough
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: DPT vaccine.

claims.subject: Whooping cough
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antibiotics, given early.

claims.subject: Whooping cough
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: Violent coughing fits; DPT vaccine prevents it.

claims.subject: Meningitis
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Meningococcus identified 1887.

claims.subject: Meningitis
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Infects the lining of the brain. Can kill a healthy person within HOURS.

claims.subject: Meningitis
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide; the African 'meningitis belt' worst.

claims.subject: Meningitis
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Meningococcal vaccine.

claims.subject: Meningitis
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Emergency antibiotics. Every hour counts.

claims.subject: Pneumonia
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Streptococcus pneumoniae, identified 1881.

claims.subject: Pneumonia
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Fills the lungs with fluid. The single biggest infectious killer of children worldwide.

claims.subject: Pneumonia
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Everywhere.

claims.subject: Pneumonia
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Pneumococcal vaccine; flu vaccine; clean cooking fuel.

claims.subject: Pneumonia
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antibiotics and oxygen.

claims.subject: Strep throat
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Group A Streptococcus.

claims.subject: Strep throat
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Sore throat. But if ignored, the antibodies you make against it can attack YOUR OWN HEART VALVES (rheumatic fever).

claims.subject: Strep throat
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide; rheumatic heart disease is a major problem in India.

claims.subject: Strep throat
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Treat sore throats properly.

claims.subject: Strep throat
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antibiotics. Which are given mainly to prevent the heart damage.

claims.subject: Leprosy
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Bacterium found by Gerhard Hansen, 1873. The first bacterium ever linked to human disease.

claims.subject: Leprosy
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Attacks the nerves. Numbness means injuries go unnoticed, and THAT causes the deformity. Not the germ eating the flesh, as people wrongly believe.

claims.subject: Leprosy
claims.label: Found
claims.text: India records a large share of the world's new cases.

claims.subject: Leprosy
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: IT IS NOT SPREAD BY TOUCH. It spreads by droplets, after months of close contact, and about 95% of people are naturally immune to it. It enters through the NOSE, which is why it is in the Nose lane and not the Contact lane. The belief that a handshake spreads leprosy is a myth that exiled people to colonies for centuries.

claims.subject: Leprosy
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Completely curable with multi-drug therapy. Free worldwide since 1995.

claims.subject: Legionnaires' disease
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Named after a 1976 outbreak at an American Legion convention.

claims.subject: Legionnaires' disease
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Severe pneumonia from bacteria in air-conditioning and water systems.

claims.subject: Legionnaires' disease
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide, in buildings with poorly maintained water systems.

claims.subject: Legionnaires' disease
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Maintain cooling towers and water tanks.

claims.subject: Legionnaires' disease
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antibiotics.

claims.subject: Diphtheria
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Antitoxin by von Behring, 1890. Winning the FIRST Nobel Prize in Medicine.

claims.subject: Diphtheria
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: A grey membrane chokes the throat, and its TOXIN attacks the heart. The toxin is pre-formed. It poisons you directly.

claims.subject: Diphtheria
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide where vaccination lapses; outbreaks still occur in India.

claims.subject: Diphtheria
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: DPT vaccine.

claims.subject: Diphtheria
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: ANTITOXIN. Antibodies. No cell can eat a toxin.

claims.subject: Mucormycosis
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: 'Black fungus'. Surged across India in 2021 among COVID patients.

claims.subject: Mucormycosis
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Invades nose and sinuses, then the eye and BRAIN. Often fatal.

claims.subject: Mucormycosis
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide, but it strikes the immunocompromised. Diabetics, steroid patients.

claims.subject: Mucormycosis
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Control diabetes; use steroids carefully.

claims.subject: Mucormycosis
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antifungals and surgery. A pure OPPORTUNIST. It only wins when your defences are already down.

claims.subject: Aspergillosis
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Aspergillus mould, described 1729.

claims.subject: Aspergillosis
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: A mould you breathe in daily. Harmless, unless your defences are weak.

claims.subject: Aspergillosis
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Everywhere: soil, dust, damp buildings.

claims.subject: Aspergillosis
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Avoid dust if immunocompromised.

claims.subject: Aspergillosis
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antifungals. Neutrophils are the key defence. Which is why neutropenia invites it in.

claims.subject: Cryptococcus
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Described 1894; a leading killer in AIDS.

claims.subject: Cryptococcus
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Fungal meningitis. It invades the BRAIN.

claims.subject: Cryptococcus
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide, in soil and pigeon droppings.

claims.subject: Cryptococcus
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Hard to avoid; the real defence is a working immune system.

claims.subject: Cryptococcus
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antifungals. Mostly attacks people with HIV.

claims.subject: Pneumocystis pneumonia
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Recognised in the 1980s as the disease that revealed AIDS.

claims.subject: Pneumocystis pneumonia
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: A fungus that only causes pneumonia when helper T-cells are destroyed.

claims.subject: Pneumocystis pneumonia
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide, in the severely immunosuppressed.

claims.subject: Pneumocystis pneumonia
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Preventive antibiotics for at-risk patients.

claims.subject: Pneumocystis pneumonia
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antibiotics/antifungals. It is a signpost of a collapsed immune system.

claims.subject: Dengue
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Four different serotypes. This matters enormously.

claims.subject: Dengue
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: High fever, severe joint pain, crashing platelets (marrow).

claims.subject: Dengue
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Tropics; a major monsoon disease across India.

claims.subject: Dengue
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Aedes mosquito control. It bites in DAYTIME. Remove standing water.

claims.subject: Dengue
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: No cure; fluids. Never give aspirin. A SECOND dengue infection can be far worse (ADE).

claims.subject: Dengue
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: Crashes the marrow's platelet supply.

claims.subject: Chikungunya
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: First described in Tanzania, 1952. The name means 'to become contorted'.

claims.subject: Chikungunya
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Fever and severe joint pain that can last months.

claims.subject: Chikungunya
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Africa, Asia, the Americas; common in India.

claims.subject: Chikungunya
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Aedes mosquito control.

claims.subject: Chikungunya
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: No antiviral; pain relief.

claims.subject: Chikungunya
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: Mosquito virus; joint pain, sometimes myocarditis.

claims.subject: Japanese encephalitis
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Virus isolated in Japan, 1935.

claims.subject: Japanese encephalitis
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Brain inflammation; often leaves permanent damage.

claims.subject: Japanese encephalitis
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Rural Asia including India; pigs and birds are the reservoir.

claims.subject: Japanese encephalitis
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: JE vaccine; mosquito control.

claims.subject: Japanese encephalitis
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: No cure. Supportive care only.

claims.subject: Japanese encephalitis
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: Mosquito-borne brain infection; vaccine-preventable.

claims.subject: Yellow fever
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Shown to be mosquito-borne by Walter Reed, 1900.

claims.subject: Yellow fever
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Fever, liver failure and jaundice (the 'yellow'), bleeding.

claims.subject: Yellow fever
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Africa and South America.

claims.subject: Yellow fever
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: One highly effective, lifelong vaccine.

claims.subject: Yellow fever
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Supportive care.

claims.subject: Yellow fever
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: Attacks the liver. Hence the jaundice.

claims.subject: Zika
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Identified 1947; caused a global emergency in 2015-16.

claims.subject: Zika
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Mild in adults. But causes severe brain defects in unborn babies.

claims.subject: Zika
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Tropics.

claims.subject: Zika
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Mosquito control; protect pregnancies.

claims.subject: Zika
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: No specific treatment.

claims.subject: West Nile fever
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Isolated in Uganda, 1937.

claims.subject: West Nile fever
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Usually mild; occasionally causes brain inflammation.

claims.subject: West Nile fever
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Africa, Europe, Americas, Asia.

claims.subject: West Nile fever
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Mosquito control.

claims.subject: West Nile fever
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Supportive care.

claims.subject: Rabies
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Vaccine by Louis Pasteur, 1885.

claims.subject: Rabies
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Creeps up your NERVES to the brain, where antibodies cannot follow. Almost 100% fatal once symptoms begin.

claims.subject: Rabies
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide; dogs are the main source in India.

claims.subject: Rabies
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Vaccinate dogs. After a bite: wash it, and get the vaccine IMMEDIATELY.

claims.subject: Rabies
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Post-exposure vaccine works BEFORE symptoms start. After that, nothing does.

claims.subject: Rabies
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: Creeps inside nerves where antibodies can't follow.

claims.subject: HIV
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Identified 1983 by Montagnier and Barré-Sinoussi (Nobel Prize).

claims.subject: HIV
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: It destroys HELPER T-CELLS. The commanders of your immune system. Without them, ordinary germs become lethal.

claims.subject: HIV
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide; ~39 million people live with HIV. Spread by unprotected sex, shared needles, and infected blood.

claims.subject: HIV
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Condoms; never share needles; screened blood; PrEP medication. It is NOT spread by mosquitoes, sharing food, or touching. A myth worth killing.

claims.subject: HIV
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antiretroviral therapy: not a cure, but people now live full lives, and treatment makes them unable to pass it on. Attacking the immune system itself is why HIV is so dangerous.

claims.subject: Hepatitis B
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Discovered by Baruch Blumberg, 1965 (Nobel Prize). First anti-cancer vaccine.

claims.subject: Hepatitis B
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Attacks the liver; can persist for life and cause liver cancer.

claims.subject: Hepatitis B
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide; ~250 million chronic carriers.

claims.subject: Hepatitis B
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Hepatitis B vaccine. Given at birth in India.

claims.subject: Hepatitis B
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antivirals control it; the vaccine prevents it.

claims.subject: Hepatitis C
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Identified 1989; Nobel Prize 2020.

claims.subject: Hepatitis C
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Silently scars the liver for decades. Cirrhosis and cancer.

claims.subject: Hepatitis C
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide.

claims.subject: Hepatitis C
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: No vaccine yet; screened blood and clean needles.

claims.subject: Hepatitis C
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: CURABLE since 2014 with direct-acting antivirals. One of medicine's great wins.

claims.subject: Chagas disease
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Discovered by Carlos Chagas, 1909. He found the parasite, the vector and the disease.

claims.subject: Chagas disease
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: A parasite that HIDES INSIDE HEART MUSCLE for decades, then destroys it.

claims.subject: Chagas disease
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Latin America.

claims.subject: Chagas disease
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Control the 'kissing bug'; improve housing.

claims.subject: Chagas disease
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Drugs work early; once the heart is damaged, it is irreversible.

claims.subject: Lyme disease
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Identified in Lyme, Connecticut, 1975.

claims.subject: Lyme disease
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Bull's-eye rash; can attack the heart (Lyme carditis) and nerves.

claims.subject: Lyme disease
claims.label: Found
claims.text: North America, Europe, parts of Asia. From tick bites.

claims.subject: Lyme disease
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Cover skin in woods; remove ticks quickly.

claims.subject: Lyme disease
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antibiotics. Very effective if caught early.

claims.subject: Lyme disease
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: Tick bite; can cause Lyme carditis in the heart.

claims.subject: Plague
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Yersinia pestis. The Black Death killed a third of Europe (1347-51).

claims.subject: Plague
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Swollen lymph nodes ('buboes'); the lung form spreads person to person and kills fast.

claims.subject: Plague
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Rare now; pockets in Africa, Asia, the Americas.

claims.subject: Plague
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Rodent and flea control.

claims.subject: Plague
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Curable with prompt antibiotics.

claims.subject: Plague
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: Flea bites. The historical Black Death.

claims.subject: Scrub typhus
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Recognised in Asia; a major cause of fever in India.

claims.subject: Scrub typhus
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Fever with a black scab at the mite bite; can cause pneumonia and brain inflammation.

claims.subject: Scrub typhus
claims.label: Found
claims.text: The 'tsutsugamushi triangle'. Including India.

claims.subject: Scrub typhus
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Avoid mite-infested scrub; protective clothing.

claims.subject: Scrub typhus
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Doxycycline. Cheap and highly effective.

claims.subject: Malaria
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Ronald Ross proved mosquitoes carry it. In Secunderabad, INDIA, 1897. Nobel Prize.

claims.subject: Malaria
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Bite → LIVER (hides inside liver cells) → bursts into blood → fever cycles, anaemia, cerebral malaria.

claims.subject: Malaria
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Tropics; still a major disease in India.

claims.subject: Malaria
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Nets, repellents, draining standing water.

claims.subject: Malaria
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antimalarials. P. vivax needs a SECOND drug to clear the liver. Or it relapses months later.

claims.subject: Malaria (blood)
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: The blood stage. Merozoites bursting out of the liver.

claims.subject: Malaria (blood)
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Invades red blood cells; causes the classic fever cycles.

claims.subject: Malaria (blood)
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Tropics.

claims.subject: Malaria (blood)
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Mosquito control.

claims.subject: Malaria (blood)
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: NOW antibodies and phagocytes can reach it. This is the stage you can actually fight.

claims.subject: Kala-azar
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Visceral leishmaniasis. Sir Upendranath Brahmachari developed the first cure. In India, 1920.

claims.subject: Kala-azar
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: HIDES INSIDE YOUR MACROPHAGES. It turns your own defender cell into its home. Destroys the spleen; fatal untreated.

claims.subject: Kala-azar
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Bihar, India, has historically carried a large share of the world's cases.

claims.subject: Kala-azar
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Sandfly control; indoor spraying.

claims.subject: Kala-azar
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Liposomal amphotericin B. India has driven cases down dramatically.

claims.subject: Sleeping sickness
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: African trypanosomiasis; the parasite was found in 1901.

claims.subject: Sleeping sickness
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: ANTIGENIC VARIATION. It keeps changing its coat, so your antibodies never quite fit. Eventually invades the brain.

claims.subject: Sleeping sickness
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Sub-Saharan Africa; spread by the tsetse fly.

claims.subject: Sleeping sickness
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Vector control.

claims.subject: Sleeping sickness
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Drugs exist, and cases have collapsed. Its trick. Changing disguise. Is why a vaccine is so hard.

claims.subject: Filariasis
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Elephantiasis; the worm was found by Patrick Manson, 1877.

claims.subject: Filariasis
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Adult worms BLOCK YOUR LYMPHATIC VESSELS. Fluid cannot drain, and limbs swell enormously.

claims.subject: Filariasis
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Tropics; India has run one of the world's largest elimination programmes.

claims.subject: Filariasis
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Mass drug administration; mosquito control.

claims.subject: Filariasis
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antiparasitic drugs kill the worms; the swelling is often permanent.

claims.subject: Snake venom
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Antivenom invented by Albert Calmette, 1895. Using antibodies from horses.

claims.subject: Snake venom
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Not alive, not a germ. A mix of toxic proteins. Attacks heart, kidneys and nerves.

claims.subject: Snake venom
claims.label: Found
claims.text: India has the world's highest snakebite death toll. Roughly 58,000 a year.

claims.subject: Snake venom
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Boots and a torch after dark; never reach blindly into grass.

claims.subject: Snake venom
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: ANTIVENOM. Borrowed antibodies. PASSIVE immunity: instant, but temporary.

claims.subject: Russell's viper venom
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: One of India's 'Big Four' snakes.

claims.subject: Russell's viper venom
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Destroys blood clotting and shreds the KIDNEYS. A leading cause of snakebite death in India.

claims.subject: Russell's viper venom
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Across the Indian subcontinent.

claims.subject: Russell's viper venom
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Boots; clear rubble near homes; torch at night.

claims.subject: Russell's viper venom
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antivenom, urgently. Dialysis may be needed for the kidneys.

claims.subject: Red scorpion sting
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Indian red scorpion. Among the most lethal scorpions in the world.

claims.subject: Red scorpion sting
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Venom floods the body with adrenaline; the HEART and LUNGS fail.

claims.subject: Red scorpion sting
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Western and southern India; a major cause of child deaths in some districts.

claims.subject: Red scorpion sting
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Shake out shoes; seal home floors.

claims.subject: Red scorpion sting
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: The drug prazosin transformed survival. An Indian medical breakthrough.

claims.subject: Tetanus
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Toxin isolated 1890 by Kitasato and von Behring.

claims.subject: Tetanus
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Its TOXIN locks the muscles rigid. 'lockjaw'. Not contagious at all.

claims.subject: Tetanus
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Soil and rusty metal, worldwide.

claims.subject: Tetanus
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Tetanus vaccine and boosters; clean wounds.

claims.subject: Tetanus
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antitoxin and intensive care. Only antibodies can neutralise a toxin.

claims.subject: Tetanus
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: A toxin that locks muscles ('lockjaw').

claims.subject: MRSA
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Methicillin-resistant Staph aureus, first seen 1961.

claims.subject: MRSA
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Skin abscesses. And in the blood it can seed ANY organ, including heart valves.

claims.subject: MRSA
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide, especially hospitals.

claims.subject: MRSA
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Hand hygiene; careful antibiotic use.

claims.subject: MRSA
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Only a few antibiotics still work. The classic superbug.

claims.subject: MRSA
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: A superbug. In the blood it can seed ANY organ, including heart valves.

claims.subject: Cellulitis
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Caused by Streptococcus or Staphylococcus.

claims.subject: Cellulitis
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Hot, red, spreading skin infection; can reach blood, bone and heart valves.

claims.subject: Cellulitis
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide.

claims.subject: Cellulitis
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Clean and cover cuts.

claims.subject: Cellulitis
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antibiotics.

claims.subject: Cellulitis
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: Staph/Strep skin infection; can settle on heart valves.

claims.subject: Leptospirosis
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Bacterium identified 1907.

claims.subject: Leptospirosis
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Fever, then kidney and liver failure (Weil's disease).

claims.subject: Leptospirosis
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Tropics; a monsoon and flood disease in India.

claims.subject: Leptospirosis
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Avoid wading in floodwater with open cuts; rodent control.

claims.subject: Leptospirosis
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antibiotics, early.

claims.subject: Leptospirosis
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: Enters through cuts in floodwater. A monsoon risk.

claims.subject: Gas gangrene
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Clostridium perfringens. Notorious in the trenches of WWI.

claims.subject: Gas gangrene
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Destroys tissue fast, producing gas; its toxins poison the kidneys.

claims.subject: Gas gangrene
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide, in deep dirty wounds.

claims.subject: Gas gangrene
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Clean deep wounds promptly.

claims.subject: Gas gangrene
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Surgery plus antibiotics. A true emergency.

claims.subject: Gas gangrene
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: Destroys deep tissue fast; a surgical emergency.

claims.subject: Syphilis
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Bacterium found 1905; the first 'magic bullet' drug (Salvarsan) targeted it.

claims.subject: Syphilis
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Progresses over years to attack the brain and heart. Can pass to an unborn baby.

claims.subject: Syphilis
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide; rising again.

claims.subject: Syphilis
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Safe practices; screening in pregnancy.

claims.subject: Syphilis
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Penicillin. Still completely effective after 80 years.

claims.subject: Brucellosis
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Traced to goat's milk by David Bruce, 1887.

claims.subject: Brucellosis
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Undulating fever; settles in the spleen, liver and bones.

claims.subject: Brucellosis
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide, from unpasteurised milk and infected livestock.

claims.subject: Brucellosis
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Pasteurise milk; vaccinate animals.

claims.subject: Brucellosis
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Long courses of antibiotics.

claims.subject: Cold sore
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Herpes simplex virus; known since antiquity.

claims.subject: Cold sore
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Blisters on the lip. Then retreats into your NERVES to hide from antibodies.

claims.subject: Cold sore
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide; most adults carry it.

claims.subject: Cold sore
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Avoid contact during an outbreak.

claims.subject: Cold sore
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antivirals shorten attacks. It is never fully cleared.

claims.subject: Cold sore
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: Retreats into nerves to hide from antibodies.

claims.subject: Human papillomavirus
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Link to cervical cancer proven by Harald zur Hausen (Nobel Prize, 2008).

claims.subject: Human papillomavirus
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Hides inside cells for years and can turn them cancerous. It causes almost ALL cervical cancer.

claims.subject: Human papillomavirus
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide; most adults meet it at some point.

claims.subject: Human papillomavirus
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: The HPV VACCINE. The first vaccine that prevents a cancer. India began rolling it out nationally; it works best given before exposure.

claims.subject: Human papillomavirus
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: No antiviral. Screening catches early changes. This is the clearest case in the whole deck of a vaccine stopping a cancer before it starts.

claims.subject: Ebola
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: First outbreak near the Ebola River, 1976.

claims.subject: Ebola
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Massive internal bleeding; liver and spleen collapse. Kills up to 90%.

claims.subject: Ebola
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Central and West Africa.

claims.subject: Ebola
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Isolation, protective equipment. And now a working vaccine.

claims.subject: Ebola
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antibody treatments and supportive care; survival has improved greatly.

claims.subject: Anthrax
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Robert Koch used it in 1876 to PROVE germs cause disease. Pasteur vaccinated sheep in 1881.

claims.subject: Anthrax
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Its TOXIN kills cells directly; the inhaled form is nearly always fatal.

claims.subject: Anthrax
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Soil worldwide; affects livestock handlers.

claims.subject: Anthrax
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Vaccinate livestock; handle hides carefully.

claims.subject: Anthrax
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antibiotics plus ANTITOXIN. The toxin must be neutralised separately.

claims.subject: Hookworm
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Linked to anaemia by Arthur Looss, 1898. He infected himself by accident.

claims.subject: Hookworm
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Burrows in through BARE SKIN, travels to the gut, and drinks your blood. Causing anaemia.

claims.subject: Hookworm
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Warm damp soil where people walk barefoot.

claims.subject: Hookworm
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Wear shoes; sanitation.

claims.subject: Hookworm
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Deworming tablets plus iron.

claims.subject: Schistosomiasis
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Worm found by Theodor Bilharz, 1851.

claims.subject: Schistosomiasis
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Larvae penetrate skin in fresh water; adult worms scar the liver and bladder.

claims.subject: Schistosomiasis
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Africa, Middle East, parts of Asia.

claims.subject: Schistosomiasis
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Avoid infested fresh water; snail control.

claims.subject: Schistosomiasis
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Praziquantel. A single effective drug.

claims.subject: Guinea worm
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Ancient. Possibly the 'fiery serpent' of the Bible.

claims.subject: Guinea worm
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: A metre-long worm slowly emerges through the skin.

claims.subject: Guinea worm
claims.label: Found
claims.text: ALMOST ERADICATED. From 3.5 million cases in 1986 to a handful today.

claims.subject: Guinea worm
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Filter drinking water. No drug, no vaccine. Just clean water.

claims.subject: Guinea worm
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Wind the worm out slowly. Proof that prevention alone can defeat a disease.

claims.subject: Histoplasmosis
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Described 1906.

claims.subject: Histoplasmosis
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: A fungus from soil with bird or bat droppings; attacks the lungs and spleen.

claims.subject: Histoplasmosis
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide, including river valleys of India.

claims.subject: Histoplasmosis
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Avoid dusty caves and bird roosts.

claims.subject: Histoplasmosis
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antifungals; often self-limiting in healthy people.

claims.subject: Typhoid
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Salmonella Typhi; 'Typhoid Mary' spread it while healthy herself.

claims.subject: Typhoid
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Prolonged high fever; infects the liver, spleen and gut.

claims.subject: Typhoid
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Where sanitation is poor. Common in South Asia.

claims.subject: Typhoid
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Clean water; typhoid conjugate vaccine.

claims.subject: Typhoid
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antibiotics. But drug-resistant typhoid is spreading in India and Pakistan.

claims.subject: Typhoid
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: Unclean water; hits liver and spleen.

claims.subject: Cholera
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: John Snow traced it to a London water pump in 1854. The birth of epidemiology.

claims.subject: Cholera
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Its TOXIN forces the gut to pour out litres of water. Dehydration kills within hours.

claims.subject: Cholera
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Outbreaks wherever water is contaminated.

claims.subject: Cholera
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Clean water and sanitation; oral vaccine.

claims.subject: Cholera
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Oral rehydration salts (ORS). Simple, cheap, and one of the great lifesavers.

claims.subject: Cholera
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: Dehydration wrecks the kidneys.

claims.subject: Dysentery
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Shigella, identified by Kiyoshi Shiga, 1897.

claims.subject: Dysentery
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Bloody diarrhoea; can damage the kidneys.

claims.subject: Dysentery
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Where hygiene is poor.

claims.subject: Dysentery
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Handwashing, clean water.

claims.subject: Dysentery
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Rehydration; antibiotics when severe.

claims.subject: Dysentery
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: Bloody diarrhoea from dirty water.

claims.subject: Food poisoning
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: E. coli described by Theodor Escherich, 1885.

claims.subject: Food poisoning
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Cramps and diarrhoea; some strains harm the kidneys.

claims.subject: Food poisoning
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide.

claims.subject: Food poisoning
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Cook food properly; wash hands.

claims.subject: Food poisoning
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Usually self-limiting; rehydration.

claims.subject: Food poisoning
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: Some E. coli damage the kidneys (HUS).

claims.subject: Listeria
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Named after Joseph Lister, 1940.

claims.subject: Listeria
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Survives refrigeration; crosses into the BRAIN and the placenta.

claims.subject: Listeria
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Soft cheeses, deli meats; worldwide.

claims.subject: Listeria
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Avoid unpasteurised dairy in pregnancy.

claims.subject: Listeria
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antibiotics.

claims.subject: Stomach ulcer (H. pylori)
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Barry Marshall DRANK the bacteria in 1984 to prove they cause ulcers. He won the Nobel Prize.

claims.subject: Stomach ulcer (H. pylori)
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Burrows into the stomach lining; causes ulcers and stomach cancer.

claims.subject: Stomach ulcer (H. pylori)
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Perhaps half the world carries it.

claims.subject: Stomach ulcer (H. pylori)
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Hygiene and clean water.

claims.subject: Stomach ulcer (H. pylori)
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antibiotics CURE it. Ulcers were once thought to be caused by stress.

claims.subject: Rotavirus
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Discovered 1973.

claims.subject: Rotavirus
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Severe diarrhoea and dehydration in young children.

claims.subject: Rotavirus
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide; a leading killer of children before vaccines.

claims.subject: Rotavirus
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Rotavirus vaccine. Now in India's immunisation programme.

claims.subject: Rotavirus
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Oral rehydration.

claims.subject: Rotavirus
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: A top cause of child diarrhoea. Vaccine-preventable.

claims.subject: Hepatitis A
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Virus identified 1973.

claims.subject: Hepatitis A
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Liver inflammation and jaundice; no chronic form.

claims.subject: Hepatitis A
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Where sanitation is poor.

claims.subject: Hepatitis A
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Vaccine; clean food and water.

claims.subject: Hepatitis A
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Rest; recovery is usually complete.

claims.subject: Hepatitis A
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: A liver virus from contaminated food or water.

claims.subject: Hepatitis E
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Recognised after outbreaks in INDIA in the 1970s-80s.

claims.subject: Hepatitis E
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Liver inflammation; especially dangerous in pregnancy.

claims.subject: Hepatitis E
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Waterborne; common in South Asia.

claims.subject: Hepatitis E
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Clean water.

claims.subject: Hepatitis E
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Supportive care.

claims.subject: Hepatitis E
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: Waterborne liver virus.

claims.subject: Norovirus
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Traced to an outbreak in Norwalk, Ohio, 1968.

claims.subject: Norovirus
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Sudden violent vomiting and diarrhoea; astonishingly contagious.

claims.subject: Norovirus
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide. Famous on cruise ships and in schools.

claims.subject: Norovirus
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Handwashing (alcohol gel works poorly here).

claims.subject: Norovirus
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Rehydration; passes in a couple of days.

claims.subject: Norovirus
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: The 'winter vomiting' bug.

claims.subject: Polio
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Vaccines by Salk (1955) and Sabin (oral, 1961).

claims.subject: Polio
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Enters through the gut; destroys nerve cells and paralyses.

claims.subject: Polio
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Nearly eradicated. INDIA was declared polio-free in 2014.

claims.subject: Polio
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Oral polio vaccine. One of the great public-health triumphs.

claims.subject: Polio
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: No cure for the paralysis. Prevention is everything.

claims.subject: Polio
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: Enters via the gut, attacks nerves.

claims.subject: Botulism
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Toxin identified 1895. The most poisonous substance known to science.

claims.subject: Botulism
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Not alive. Paralyses every muscle, including breathing. A few nanograms can kill.

claims.subject: Botulism
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Improperly canned or preserved food.

claims.subject: Botulism
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Proper canning; never feed honey to infants.

claims.subject: Botulism
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: ANTITOXIN. (In tiny doses this same toxin is Botox.)

claims.subject: Shiga toxin (E. coli O157)
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Named after Kiyoshi Shiga.

claims.subject: Shiga toxin (E. coli O157)
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Not alive. Destroys the KIDNEYS (haemolytic uraemic syndrome), especially in children.

claims.subject: Shiga toxin (E. coli O157)
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Undercooked beef, unpasteurised milk.

claims.subject: Shiga toxin (E. coli O157)
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Cook meat thoroughly.

claims.subject: Shiga toxin (E. coli O157)
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Supportive care and dialysis. Antibiotics can make it WORSE by releasing more toxin.

claims.subject: Roundworm
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Ascaris lumbricoides. Grows up to 35 cm long.

claims.subject: Roundworm
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Larvae migrate THROUGH THE LUNGS, then return to the gut. Can block the intestines.

claims.subject: Roundworm
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Where sanitation is poor. One of the commonest infections on Earth.

claims.subject: Roundworm
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Sanitation; deworming programmes.

claims.subject: Roundworm
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Deworming tablets. Too big for any cell to swallow.

claims.subject: Tapeworm
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Neurocysticercosis recognised as a major cause of epilepsy.

claims.subject: Tapeworm
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Larvae form cysts IN THE BRAIN. A leading cause of adult-onset epilepsy in India.

claims.subject: Tapeworm
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Where pigs are raised with poor sanitation.

claims.subject: Tapeworm
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Cook pork thoroughly; sanitation; handwashing.

claims.subject: Tapeworm
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antiparasitic drugs plus anti-seizure medicine.

claims.subject: Whipworm
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Trichuris trichiura.

claims.subject: Whipworm
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Burrows into the gut wall; causes chronic blood loss and anaemia in children.

claims.subject: Whipworm
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Warm, humid regions worldwide.

claims.subject: Whipworm
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Sanitation; handwashing.

claims.subject: Whipworm
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Deworming tablets.

claims.subject: Amoebiasis
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Entamoeba histolytica. The species name means 'tissue-dissolving'.

claims.subject: Amoebiasis
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Eats through the gut wall and forms a LIVER ABSCESS.

claims.subject: Amoebiasis
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Common in India and other tropical regions.

claims.subject: Amoebiasis
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Clean water; wash vegetables.

claims.subject: Amoebiasis
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Metronidazole; the abscess may need draining.

claims.subject: Giardia
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Seen by Antonie van Leeuwenhoek in 1681. In his own stool.

claims.subject: Giardia
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Coats the gut and blocks absorption. You eat, but you starve. Draining your energy.

claims.subject: Giardia
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide; 'beaver fever' from streams and unclean water.

claims.subject: Giardia
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Filter or boil water.

claims.subject: Giardia
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antiparasitic drugs.

claims.subject: Toxoplasmosis
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Identified 1908.

claims.subject: Toxoplasmosis
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Forms silent CYSTS IN THE BRAIN and hides there for life. Dangerous to unborn babies and to people with AIDS.

claims.subject: Toxoplasmosis
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide. From undercooked meat and cat faeces.

claims.subject: Toxoplasmosis
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Cook meat; pregnant women should avoid cat litter.

claims.subject: Toxoplasmosis
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Drugs only when it reactivates.

claims.subject: Candida
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: A yeast that lives on almost everyone, harmlessly.

claims.subject: Candida
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Normally kept in check by your immune system and your other microbes. But if either falls, it invades ANY organ.

claims.subject: Candida
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Everywhere. It is already on you right now.

claims.subject: Candida
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Careful antibiotic use. Killing your good bacteria lets Candida bloom.

claims.subject: Candida
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antifungals. The classic OPPORTUNIST.

claims.subject: Scabies
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: The mite was seen under a microscope in 1687. Making scabies one of the FIRST diseases ever proven to have a specific cause.

claims.subject: Scabies
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: A mite that burrows into your skin and lays eggs. The unbearable itch is an ALLERGIC reaction to it. Your own immune system causing the misery.

claims.subject: Scabies
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide; ~200 million people at any moment. Spreads by prolonged skin-to-skin contact and shared bedding.

claims.subject: Scabies
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Treat the whole household at once, and wash all bedding.

claims.subject: Scabies
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Permethrin cream or ivermectin. Cheap and curable. But it keeps coming back if only one person is treated.

claims.subject: Ringworm
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Not a worm at all. A FUNGUS. The name comes from the ring-shaped rash.

claims.subject: Ringworm
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: A fungus digesting the keratin in your skin, hair and nails.

claims.subject: Ringworm
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Everywhere. Spreads by touch, shared towels, and from animals.

claims.subject: Ringworm
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Do not share towels or combs; keep skin dry.

claims.subject: Ringworm
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antifungal cream. The commonest fungal infection on Earth. And one of the most misnamed.

claims.subject: Impetigo
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Streptococcus or Staphylococcus on the skin.

claims.subject: Impetigo
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Golden crusted sores, mainly in children. Highly contagious by touch. Can lead to kidney damage.

claims.subject: Impetigo
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide; common where it is hot and crowded.

claims.subject: Impetigo
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Wash hands and cuts; do not share towels.

claims.subject: Impetigo
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antibiotic cream or tablets.

claims.subject: Trachoma
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Chlamydia trachomatis. The SAME species that causes the sexually transmitted infection, arriving by a completely different route.

claims.subject: Trachoma
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Repeated infection scars the eyelid until the lashes turn INWARD and scrape the eye. Blindness comes slowly, over years.

claims.subject: Trachoma
claims.label: Found
claims.text: The world's leading INFECTIOUS cause of blindness. India has fought a long campaign against it.

claims.subject: Trachoma
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Face-washing and clean water. The 'SAFE' strategy. Flies spread it between children's eyes.

claims.subject: Trachoma
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: A single dose of azithromycin. Surgery for the eyelid. **A disease of poverty, cured by soap and water.**

claims.subject: Conjunctivitis
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Adenovirus. 'pink eye'.

claims.subject: Conjunctivitis
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Red, weeping, gritty eyes. Astonishingly contagious: rub your eye, touch a door handle, and the next person has it.

claims.subject: Conjunctivitis
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide; sweeps through schools.

claims.subject: Conjunctivitis
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Wash hands. Do not share towels or pillows.

claims.subject: Conjunctivitis
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Usually clears itself. A NAKED virus. No envelope, so it survives on surfaces for days and hand-gel works poorly on it.

claims.subject: Molluscum contagiosum
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: A poxvirus. A distant cousin of smallpox.

claims.subject: Molluscum contagiosum
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Small pearly bumps, spread by skin contact and shared towels. Harmless but stubborn.

claims.subject: Molluscum contagiosum
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide; common in children.

claims.subject: Molluscum contagiosum
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Do not share towels; cover the bumps.

claims.subject: Molluscum contagiosum
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Usually clears on its own. But it can take a year. Your immune system gets there eventually.

claims.subject: Endocarditis
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Infection of the heart valves. Described by William Osler, 1885.

claims.subject: Endocarditis
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Bacteria in the bloodstream settle on a HEART VALVE and build a colony there, where blood flow shields them from your immune cells.

claims.subject: Endocarditis
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide. A risk after dental work, IV drug use, or a contaminated line. And after rheumatic fever has damaged a valve.

claims.subject: Endocarditis
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Treat bloodstream infections early; look after damaged valves.

claims.subject: Endocarditis
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Weeks of intravenous antibiotics; sometimes surgery to replace the valve.

claims.subject: Gonorrhoea
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Bacterium found by Albert Neisser, 1879.

claims.subject: Gonorrhoea
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Infects the reproductive tract; can spread to joints and heart valves. Often causes NO symptoms. So it spreads silently.

claims.subject: Gonorrhoea
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide; about 82 million new cases a year.

claims.subject: Gonorrhoea
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Condoms; testing and treating partners.

claims.subject: Gonorrhoea
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antibiotics. But it has now defeated almost every antibiotic we have. The WHO lists it as a PRIORITY superbug. This is antibiotic resistance happening in real time.

claims.subject: Chlamydia
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Chlamydia trachomatis. The same species that causes trachoma, the leading infectious cause of blindness.

claims.subject: Chlamydia
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: An INTRACELLULAR bacterium. It lives inside your cells, where antibodies struggle to reach. Usually silent; can cause infertility.

claims.subject: Chlamydia
claims.label: Found
claims.text: The commonest bacterial STI in the world.

claims.subject: Chlamydia
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Condoms; routine screening.

claims.subject: Chlamydia
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antibiotics. Easy to cure. But only if you know you have it.

claims.subject: Genital herpes
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Herpes simplex virus type 2.

claims.subject: Genital herpes
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Like a cold sore, it retreats into your NERVES and hides there for life. Antibodies cannot follow it in.

claims.subject: Genital herpes
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide; extremely common.

claims.subject: Genital herpes
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Condoms reduce but do not eliminate the risk.

claims.subject: Genital herpes
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antivirals control outbreaks. It is never cleared. A lifelong passenger.

claims.subject: Trichomoniasis
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: A single-celled protozoan parasite, described 1836.

claims.subject: Trichomoniasis
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: The commonest curable STI on Earth. Often silent.

claims.subject: Trichomoniasis
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide. Around 156 million cases a year.

claims.subject: Trichomoniasis
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Condoms; treating partners.

claims.subject: Trichomoniasis
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: A single course of metronidazole cures it.

claims.subject: Hepatitis D
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Identified 1977. The strangest virus in this deck.

claims.subject: Hepatitis D
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: It is INCOMPLETE. It cannot infect you on its own: it can ONLY survive if Hepatitis B is already there, because it borrows Hep B's outer coat. A virus that parasitises another virus.

claims.subject: Hepatitis D
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Wherever Hepatitis B is; the most severe form of viral hepatitis.

claims.subject: Hepatitis D
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: The Hepatitis B vaccine ALSO prevents Hepatitis D. Block the host and the passenger cannot land.

claims.subject: Hepatitis D
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Hard to treat. Prevention through the Hep B vaccine is the real answer.

claims.subject: Transfusion malaria
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Malaria delivered straight into the bloodstream by transfused blood.

claims.subject: Transfusion malaria
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: It SKIPS the mosquito and skips the tissues. It goes directly to the liver.

claims.subject: Transfusion malaria
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Anywhere blood is not properly screened.

claims.subject: Transfusion malaria
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Screening donated blood. Which is why blood banks test every unit.

claims.subject: Transfusion malaria
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antimalarials. This is why safe transfusion is a public-health issue, not just a hospital one.

claims.subject: Catheter sepsis
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: A fungal bloodstream infection from a drip line or catheter.

claims.subject: Catheter sepsis
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Candida travelling up a plastic tube straight into your blood, bypassing every barrier you have.

claims.subject: Catheter sepsis
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Hospitals worldwide. One of the commonest hospital-acquired infections.

claims.subject: Catheter sepsis
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Sterile technique; remove lines as soon as they are not needed.

claims.subject: Catheter sepsis
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antifungals. A reminder that medicine itself can open a door.

claims.subject: Cannula infection
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Bacteria entering through a drip needle.

claims.subject: Cannula infection
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Staph from the skin, pushed straight into the bloodstream by a needle. Can seed the heart valves.

claims.subject: Cannula infection
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Hospitals worldwide.

claims.subject: Cannula infection
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Clean the skin; change the line; wash hands.

claims.subject: Cannula infection
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antibiotics. And remove the line.

claims.subject: Tetanus toxin
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Isolated 1890.

claims.subject: Tetanus toxin
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Not alive. Locks the muscles rigid. It does not reproduce. It simply poisons.

claims.subject: Tetanus toxin
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Released by tetanus bacteria in a wound.

claims.subject: Tetanus toxin
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Tetanus vaccine trains you to make ANTITOXIN.

claims.subject: Tetanus toxin
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Only antibodies can neutralise it. No cell can eat a toxin.

claims.subject: Cholera toxin
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: The reason cholera kills.

claims.subject: Cholera toxin
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Not alive. Forces gut cells to pump out water; the kidneys fail from dehydration.

claims.subject: Cholera toxin
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Released by cholera bacteria.

claims.subject: Cholera toxin
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Clean water.

claims.subject: Cholera toxin
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Rehydration; antibodies neutralise the toxin.

claims.subject: Clostridial toxin
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: The toxin of gas gangrene.

claims.subject: Clostridial toxin
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Not alive. Destroys tissue and poisons the kidneys and liver.

claims.subject: Clostridial toxin
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Deep dirty wounds.

claims.subject: Clostridial toxin
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Clean wounds promptly.

claims.subject: Clostridial toxin
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antitoxin, surgery, antibiotics.

claims.subject: Diphtheria toxin
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: The toxin von Behring made the first antitoxin against.

claims.subject: Diphtheria toxin
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Not alive. Poisons the HEART muscle directly.

claims.subject: Diphtheria toxin
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Released by diphtheria bacteria.

claims.subject: Diphtheria toxin
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: DPT vaccine.

claims.subject: Diphtheria toxin
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antitoxin. Antibodies, urgently.

claims.subject: Shingles
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Recognised as reactivated chickenpox, 1953.

claims.subject: Shingles
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: The chickenpox virus hid in your nerves for decades and re-emerged.

claims.subject: Shingles
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Anyone who has had chickenpox.

claims.subject: Shingles
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Shingles vaccine.

claims.subject: Shingles
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antivirals. Proof that some viruses never truly leave.

claims.subject: Dengue (ADE)
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Antibody-dependent enhancement, described in the 1970s.

claims.subject: Dengue (ADE)
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Your antibodies from a PREVIOUS dengue do not neutralise this serotype. They HELP it into your cells.

claims.subject: Dengue (ADE)
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Tropics.

claims.subject: Dengue (ADE)
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Mosquito control. This is exactly why a dengue vaccine is so hard to make.

claims.subject: Dengue (ADE)
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antibodies will NOT work here. Use cells.

claims.subject: Malaria (relapse)
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Hypnozoites described 1982.

claims.subject: Malaria (relapse)
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: A dormant form of P. vivax slept in your liver and woke months later. From nothing.

claims.subject: Malaria (relapse)
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Wherever P. vivax occurs, including India.

claims.subject: Malaria (relapse)
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Finish the full course of primaquine to clear the liver.

claims.subject: Malaria (relapse)
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: A second drug is needed specifically for the liver forms.

claims.subject: Tuberculosis (reactivated)
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Latency has been known since the 19th century.

claims.subject: Tuberculosis (reactivated)
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: TB you thought you had beaten was only sleeping. It woke when your defences fell.

claims.subject: Tuberculosis (reactivated)
claims.label: Found
claims.text: About a quarter of the world carries latent TB.

claims.subject: Tuberculosis (reactivated)
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Treat latent TB in high-risk people.

claims.subject: Tuberculosis (reactivated)
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Months of combination antibiotics.

claims.subject: Pneumococcal pneumonia
claims.label: Discovered
claims.text: Streptococcus pneumoniae, 1881.

claims.subject: Pneumococcal pneumonia
claims.label: Causes
claims.text: Moves into lungs stripped bare by influenza. This. Not the flu itself. Killed most victims in 1918.

claims.subject: Pneumococcal pneumonia
claims.label: Found
claims.text: Worldwide.

claims.subject: Pneumococcal pneumonia
claims.label: Prevent
claims.text: Pneumococcal and flu vaccines.

claims.subject: Pneumococcal pneumonia
claims.label: Treat
claims.text: Antibiotics.

parts.title: Part 2 — The pathogen types
parts.blurb: What the app tells a player about each kind of invader, and how it is beaten. These sentences name our playing pieces (Monocyte, Killer T-Cell) but they are making a claim about immunology, not about the rules.

claims.subject: Virus
claims.label: How it is beaten
claims.text: Antibody neutralises it, or the Monocyte engulfs it. If it hides inside a cell, only the Killer T-Cell or NK Cell can reach it.

claims.subject: Virus
claims.label: In How to play
claims.text: Neutralise with a matching antibody, or the Monocyte engulfs it.

claims.subject: Virus
claims.label: In How to play
claims.text: If it hides inside a cell, only the Killer T-Cell or NK Cell can reach it.

claims.subject: Hidden Virus
claims.label: How it is beaten
claims.text: It is INSIDE one of your cells. Antibodies cannot reach it there. Killer T-Cell (never misses) or NK Cell (d6 3+). Not all of these are viruses: Toxoplasmosis and Chagas disease are PROTOZOA that live inside your cells, which is why a Killer T-Cell is the answer for them too.

claims.subject: Hidden Virus
claims.label: In How to play
claims.text: It is inside one of your own cells, where antibodies cannot go. Killer T-Cell (never misses) or NK Cell (3 or more).

claims.subject: Hidden Virus
claims.label: In How to play
claims.text: Not all are viruses: Toxoplasmosis and Chagas are protozoa that live inside cells.

claims.subject: Bacteria
claims.label: How it is beaten
claims.text: Coat it with a matching antibody, then engulf it. Or trap the swarm in a Neutrophil NET. It divides if you ignore it!

claims.subject: Bacteria
claims.label: In How to play
claims.text: Coat it with a matching antibody, then engulf it, or trap the swarm in a NET. It divides if you ignore it.

claims.subject: Bacteria
claims.label: In How to play
claims.text: Up to 8 can pack into one space.

claims.subject: Toxin
claims.label: How it is beaten
claims.text: It is NOT alive. No cell can eat it, trap it or snipe it. ANTITOXIN antibodies are the only defence (2 AP to neutralise).

claims.subject: Toxin
claims.label: In How to play
claims.text: Not alive: nothing can eat it, trap it or snipe it. Antitoxin antibodies only, and neutralising costs 2 AP.

claims.subject: Venom
claims.label: How it is beaten
claims.text: It is NOT alive and acts far too fast for your B-cells. Only an ANTIVENOM dose works. You cannot make antibodies in time.

claims.subject: Venom
claims.label: In How to play
claims.text: Not alive, and far too fast for your B-cells. Only a ready-made antivenom dose works.

claims.subject: Fungus
claims.label: How it is beaten
claims.text: It CANNOT be coated. Antibodies do not opsonise fungi here. The Monocyte engulfs it directly (it has 2 HP, so that chips it), and a Neutrophil NET kills it outright. Fungi are an INNATE problem: neutrophils and macrophages do this work.

claims.subject: Fungus
claims.label: In How to play
claims.text: It cannot be coated. The Monocyte engulfs it directly (2 hits, so that chips it) and a NET kills it outright.

claims.subject: Worm
claims.label: How it is beaten
claims.text: Too big to swallow and immune to NETs. COAT it with an antibody, then the Eosinophil strikes (2 dmg) or degranulates (3 dmg, 2 AP, and it burns the organ).

claims.subject: Worm
claims.label: In How to play
claims.text: Too big to swallow and immune to NETs. Coat it, then the Eosinophil strikes (2) or degranulates (3).

claims.subject: Worm
claims.label: In How to play
claims.text: It lodges in an organ and chews it every 3 turns.

claims.subject: Malaria
claims.label: How it is beaten
claims.text: In the blood: antibodies or the Monocyte. Inside liver cells: only the Killer T-Cell or NK Cell can reach it.

claims.subject: Malaria
claims.label: In How to play
claims.text: Three stages. Travelling in the blood: antibodies or the Monocyte. Inside liver cells: Killer T-Cell or NK Cell only. Back in the blood: antibodies again.

claims.subject: Malaria
claims.label: In How to play
claims.text: The card has the stages.

claims.subject: Parasite
claims.label: How it is beaten
claims.text: Coat it, then STRIKE it down with the Eosinophil (2 dmg) or Monocyte (1 dmg). Once it is on its last HP the Monocyte can finally engulf it. NETs do not hold it.

claims.subject: Parasite
claims.label: In How to play
claims.text: Coat it, then strike it down: Eosinophil 2 damage, Monocyte 1.

claims.subject: Parasite
claims.label: In How to play
claims.text: Once it is on its last hit point the Monocyte can finally swallow it.

parts.title: Part 3 — The cells
parts.blurb: Seven cells a player commands, each with a card, and seven resident macrophages named for the tissue they live in. **Fourteen named cell types in total.** A cell name is repeated more often than any sentence in the app, because it is what the player calls the piece for the whole game, so a wrong name is the most-repeated error available to us.

claims.subject: Monocyte
claims.label: The name we use
claims.text: The app calls this piece the Monocyte, for the real-world macrophage.

claims.subject: Monocyte
claims.label: What it does
claims.text: The big eater. It engulfs one pathogen at a time, the first each turn free and then 1 Action Point each, and every meal raises antigen presentation, the bridge that switches on the adaptive cells.

claims.subject: Monocyte
claims.label: Where it comes from
claims.text: Made in the marrow. It circulates in the blood as a monocyte and enters tissue where it is needed, maturing into a macrophage there. In the game it starts in the Bloodstream and goes wherever you send it.

claims.subject: Monocyte
claims.label: What it is best against
claims.text: Viruses and coated bacteria on its own space, and blood-stage malaria. It cannot swallow a worm or a full-strength protozoan. Those are physically too big and must be struck down first.

claims.subject: Monocyte
claims.label: What happens without it
claims.text: Without phagocytes, bacteria and fungi are never cleared, and nothing is ever presented to the adaptive team, so antibodies and killer cells never get their start.

claims.subject: Monocyte
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: A macrophage can engulf tuberculosis bacteria and still fail to kill them. It takes a helper T-cell signal to finish the job, which is why tuberculosis wakes up when helper T-cell counts fall.

claims.subject: Monocyte
claims.label: In How to play
claims.text: Engulf: free once a turn, then 1 AP. Swallows a virus, a coated bacterium, a fungus, blood-stage malaria, or a parasite already down to its last hit point.

claims.subject: Monocyte
claims.label: In How to play
claims.text: Strike: 1 damage to a coated worm or parasite.

claims.subject: Neutrophil
claims.label: The name we use
claims.text: The app calls this piece the Neutrophil, for the real-world neutrophil.

claims.subject: Neutrophil
claims.label: What it does
claims.text: The first responder. It swarms a site and destroys every living microbe standing there at once. Then it is spent, and the marrow takes four turns to replace it, or two with a primed Helper T-Cell in the Bloodstream.

claims.subject: Neutrophil
claims.label: Where it comes from
claims.text: The bloodstream, in enormous numbers: the most abundant white cell in the body, made and replaced by the marrow continuously. In the game it starts in the Bloodstream and moves two steps per Action Point.

claims.subject: Neutrophil
claims.label: What it is best against
claims.text: A swarm: bacteria, fungi and viruses standing together on one space. Not worms, not toxins, and nothing hiding inside one of your own cells.

claims.subject: Neutrophil
claims.label: What happens without it
claims.text: Neutropenia, too few neutrophils, as after chemotherapy, leaves the body open to bacterial and fungal infections that are normally stopped within hours.

claims.subject: Neutrophil
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: Neutrophils live only a day or so, and the marrow makes about a hundred billion of them every day. Their NETs are webs of their own DNA, thrown out to trap and kill microbes.

claims.subject: Neutrophil
claims.label: In How to play
claims.text: NET: traps every living microbe on its own space.

claims.subject: Neutrophil
claims.label: In How to play
claims.text: Then it is spent and returns after 4 turns, or 2 if a primed Helper T-Cell is in the bloodstream.

claims.subject: B-Cell
claims.label: The name we use
claims.text: The app calls this piece the B-Cell, for the real-world bcell.

claims.subject: B-Cell
claims.label: What it does
claims.text: The antibody factory. It produces antibodies of one class at a time; the antibodies then coat or neutralise pathogens of that class wherever they are.

claims.subject: B-Cell
claims.label: Where it comes from
claims.text: Made in the marrow (the B). In the game it starts in the Bloodstream and produces from wherever it stands, best beside a primed Helper T-Cell, which adds one antibody per action.

claims.subject: B-Cell
claims.label: What it is best against
claims.text: Anything with an antigen class. Its antibodies tag bacteria, worms and parasites so other cells can attack them, and neutralise viruses and toxins outright. A novel antigen is out of reach until clonal selection finds the one clone that fits it.

claims.subject: B-Cell
claims.label: What happens without it
claims.text: No B-cells means no antibodies: bacteria and toxins outside cells run unchecked, and there is nothing for a vaccine to build on. The human version is X-linked agammaglobulinaemia.

claims.subject: B-Cell
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: Your body already carries B-cells for antigens it has never met. Finding the one that fits a new pathogen, clonal selection, is why a first response takes days, and why the second time is fast.

claims.subject: B-Cell
claims.label: In How to play
claims.text: Never moves. Produce antibodies of one antigen class.

claims.subject: B-Cell
claims.label: In How to play
claims.text: Coat a bacterium, worm or parasite. Neutralise a virus, or a toxin for 2 AP. Vaccinate, 5 AP in total. Search for the clone, 3 AP, for Pathogen X.

claims.subject: Killer T-Cell
claims.label: The name we use
claims.text: The app calls this piece the Killer T-Cell, for the real-world tcell.

claims.subject: Killer T-Cell
claims.label: What it does
claims.text: The sniper. It kills infected cells, anything hiding inside one of your own cells, from a distance, and it never misses.

claims.subject: Killer T-Cell
claims.label: Where it comes from
claims.text: Matured in the thymus (the T), then circulating. In the game it starts in the Bloodstream and strikes along its own route or branch within its range: 3 on Training, 2 on Normal and Hard, +1 beside a primed Helper T-Cell.

claims.subject: Killer T-Cell
claims.label: What it is best against
claims.text: Hidden viruses and the protozoa that live inside cells: Toxoplasma, Chagas, liver-stage malaria, a parasite inside a resident macrophage. Useless against anything out in the open.

claims.subject: Killer T-Cell
claims.label: What happens without it
claims.text: Without killer T-cells, a virus that hides inside cells is never cleared, because the infected cell is never destroyed. Reactivating viruses like shingles are what a weakened T-cell system lets through.

claims.subject: Killer T-Cell
claims.label: Card fact
claims.text: A killer T-cell recognises an infected cell by the fragments of virus that cell displays on its own surface. The cell reports its own infection.

claims.subject: Killer T-Cell
claims.label: In How to play
claims.text: Snipe: destroys a pathogen hiding inside one of your cells. Never misses.

claims.subject: Killer T-Cell
claims.label: In How to play
claims.text: Range 3 on Training, 2 on Normal and Hard, +1 while a primed Helper stands with it.

claims.subject: Helper T-Cell
claims.label: The name we use
claims.text: The app calls this piece the Helper T-Cell, for the real-world helper.

claims.subject: Helper T-Cell
claims.label: What it does
claims.text: The conductor. It kills nothing and takes no attacking action; it licenses other cells by standing with them, but only once it has been primed by antigen presentation.

claims.subject: Helper T-Cell
claims.label: Where it comes from
claims.text: The Bloodstream at the start. Where it stands afterwards is the whole game: beside the B-Cell, beside the Killer T-Cell, beside the Eosinophil, or parked in the blood.

claims.subject: Helper T-Cell
claims.label: What it is best against
claims.text: Nothing directly. Beside the B-Cell: +1 antibody per action. Beside the Killer T-Cell: +1 range. Beside the Eosinophil: +1 step. Standing in the Bloodstream: the Neutrophil returns in 2 turns instead of 4.

claims.subject: Helper T-Cell
claims.label: What happens without it
claims.text: HIV destroys helper T-cells, and the whole adaptive system collapses with them. That is what AIDS is: not the virus's own damage but the loss of the coordinating layer, leaving the body open to infections it would normally handle easily.

claims.subject: Helper T-Cell
claims.label: Card fact
